I’m Henry, a software and AI engineer based in Lagos, Nigeria, with a background in Computer Science Education at Tai Solarin University of Education (TASUED, class of 2026).

My interests sit at the intersection of AI for learning, reliable AI systems, and real-world impact. I built LeAi as a personal project to help students learn from their own course materials. At QwamPay, I’ve worked on backend systems and AI-assisted financial operations.

I want to bring that experience into graduate research: studying how we can make intelligent systems more grounded, useful, and accessible to the people who depend on them.

Manuscript in preparation2026

Time-Series AI-Driven Congestion Management in Enterprise Campus Networks: A Simulation Using Cisco Packet Tracer and REST APIs

Henry Oderinde · Final-year project

Combining network telemetry and an LSTM model to predict congestion and inform routing and quality-of-service decisions in a simulated campus network.

Project details

The project connects a Cisco Packet Tracer controller to a Node.js / Express service through REST APIs. An LSTM model uses telemetry observations to classify congestion, with model output informing OSPF cost and QoS recommendations.

The project used 17,280 telemetry observations and reported 93.22% classification accuracy. Full evaluation details will accompany the manuscript.

Manuscript and full paper not yet publicly available.

Selected projects

From ideas to working systems
Personal project · AI for education

LeAi

I built LeAi to help students prepare for exams using the materials they already have. It turns PDFs, documents, slides, and scanned notes into grounded practice assessments through retrieval-augmented generation and OCR.

4,000+ students served · Developed through four product iterations and CcHUB incubation.

My contribution

I built the retrieval, OCR, prompt, and data pipelines, launched the first version in a month, and led product iterations. Caching and removing redundant calls reduced server requests by about 90% during a launch-day traffic surge.

QwamPay

Backend and AI engineering for financial operations: a unified operations platform, retrieval-based support assistance, and conversational banking through secure WhatsApp integrations.

300+ API operations across customer management, finance, KYC, approvals, and provider operations.

My contribution

I built systems for AI-assisted support triage, summaries, and reply drafting, alongside WhatsApp conversational banking. The backend includes PII masking, encrypted records, role-based access, approval workflows, and audit logs.
